analysis: Examined base-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md lines 822-1621 (deadline admission, MTP, sampling, tool parsers, vision caps, MiMo native paths). This is documentation only. The head-side changes (632-638: rate freshness anchored to the newest observation, so an older receipt cannot move freshness backward; 882-918: TTFT admission estimator corrections gated by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0, with decode priced per batch step; 1780: a single-line change) affect performance and deadline estimation. They do not change encryption, attestation, authorization, cache scoping or the at-rest prefix-cache posture. T-041 and SEC-035 are unaffected: the documented changes alter neither cacheSalt plumbing nor the TTL. The changed estimators could affect admission and availability (T-010/T-029 class). However, these are provider-local scheduling heuristics, and a malicious provider already controls them. A consumer could influence step shape only through ordinary requests, and actual deadline expiry and physical admission still apply per the documentation. The full head patch excerpt was truncated, and the implementation (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift) was not supplied, so the estimator safety bound cannot be verified. No security regression was identified in the supplied documentation.
